_meta.project: instex IMAGER mode -- reference constants: band menu (one wavelength per band for lambda/D), Moon angular size, Moffat beta for seeing, Airy FWHM
_meta.companion: data/imaging/constants.md (same content in Markdown, in the spirit of data/round4/mosfire.md)
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/constants/. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts or cross-checks). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text.
_meta.quote_normalisation: pdftotext (layout, raw, default) and tag-stripped HTML text (visible text and tooltip attributes); NFKC, primes/curly quotes, dashes/minus signs, tilde-operator and mu normalised; whitespace collapsed; pieces that differ only in spacing are accepted; " ... " joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows are quoted as whitespace-separated cells; OCR text (ADS scans) quoted as OCR'd.
_meta.units: SVO wavelengths in Angstrom (1 um = 10^4 A).
_meta.quote_check: 225 quote pieces (including double-quoted fragments inside notes) checked against the saved files: 0 failures

band_definition.choice: lambda_pivot (SVO "λ pivot", Calculated column) for every band
band_definition.why: One definition across all 16 bands. (1) The pivot wavelength depends on the passband only (no source spectrum), and Bessell & Murphy (2012) recommend it for describing a filter system. (2) SVO adopts it as each filter's reference wavelength (lambda_ref = lambda_pivot). (3) Recomputing from the saved curves shows SVO evaluates the pivot on the photon-counting response for both detector types (curve as given for photon counters, T/lambda for the energy-counter Bessell and NSFCam curves), so the same definition applies to every row. SVO's lambda_mean is instead computed on the energy-counting response; it differs from the pivot by +0.04% (M') to +1.35% (R), which does not matter for lambda/D.

quotes.quote: We recommend the retention of only two, the pivot wavelength, λp , that is a property of the passband only, and the isophotal wavelength
The pivot wavelength should be used as part of a description of the filter system
Reference wavelength. Defined as the same than the pivot wavelength.

quotes.loc: VOTable, PARAM WavelengthPivot <DESCRIPTION> (SVO labels this description "Peak wavelength"; the formula is the pivot)

quotes.quote: Mean wavelength. Defined as integ[x*filter(x) dx]/integ[filter(x) dx]
Full width at half maximum. Defined as the difference between the two wavelengths for which filter transmission is half maximum
Equivalent to the horizontal size of a rectangle with height equal to maximum transmission and with the same area that the one covered by the filter

quotes.loc: browse page, tooltip of the λ mean / λ cen / FWHM properties
quotes.quote: Filter transmission is transformed to "energy counter" for these calculations, that is, the photon count transmission is multiplied by λ and normalized so that peak transmission is equal to 1.

band_definition.caveat: The SVO tooltip text quoted above also appears under λ pivot, but the saved curves show the pivot is NOT evaluated on the energy-normalised curve: SVO's pivot equals sqrt(int lambda T_ph / int T_ph/lambda) with T_ph the photon-counting response (agreement to the 0.01 A printed, all 16 bands, DERIVED), whereas lambda_mean, lambda_cen, FWHM and W_eff do use the energy-counting response.
band_definition.width_choice: Tooltip width = SVO FWHM; the half-maximum band edges are lambda_cen -/+ FWHM/2 (DERIVED). W_eff (equivalent rectangle width) is listed too; W_eff/FWHM ranges from 0.83 (2MASS J, shoulder near half maximum) to 1.17 (SDSS z, long red tail).

beta_kolmogorov.unit: dimensionless (Moffat beta best matching the Kolmogorov long-exposure seeing PSF)
beta_kolmogorov.loc: Sec. 2.4 "The ability of the Moffat function to match the atmospheric turbulence prediction of the PSF"
beta_kolmogorov.quote: For a given FWHM, we have evaluated the value of β that minimizes the difference between the prediction of the atmospheric turbulence theory and the Moffat function by minimizing the χ2 of the fit between both PSFs. An optimum value of β ~ 4.765 was found.

context_quotes.quote: shown to provide the best fit to the PSF predicted from atmospheric turbulence theory when β ~ 4.765
The theory of atmospheric turbulence predicts the PSF to be the Fourier transform of exp[-(kb)5/3 ] (Fried 1966; Woolf 1982), where FWHM = 2.9207006b and b is a scaling parameter.
using a Moffat function with a b value of 4.765

beta_kolmogorov.derived: DERIVED check (Hankel transform of exp[-(kb)^(5/3)]): FWHM = 2.9207006 b (T01: 2.9207006 b). Best Moffat at the same FWHM, both normalised to unit total flux, r < 3 FWHM: beta = 4.734 (unweighted chi2) / 4.770 (r-weighted). If instead both are normalised to unit PEAK, the best beta is 6.21; T01 does not state its normalisation, but its Eq. (1) Moffat is flux-normalised and the unit-flux fit reproduces 4.765, so the number is tied to that fitting convention.

beta_common.unit: dimensionless (the usual default/empirical choice; real PSFs have broader wings than Kolmogorov theory)
beta_common.quote: current packages of data reduction in IRAF suggest a default value of β = 2.5

alternatives.quote: An elliptical Moffat function with a beta parameter of 2.5.
alternatives.note: DAOPHOT also offers moffat15 ("An elliptical Moffat function with a beta parameter of 1.5."); the daopars default function is gauss: ".ls function = "gauss""
current IRAF imexamine has no fixed default beta

alternatives.quote: For the values of β typically present in real images (2.5 < β < 4; see Saglia et al. 1993)
β=5 (to simulate the turbulence prediction), 2.5 (the default value of the IRAF package), and 1.5 (to model a large "wing" in the PSF)

beta_common.note: The word "default" is T01's ("suggest a default value of β = 2.5"); in the IRAF sources saved here 2.5 is the fixed beta of the DAOPHOT moffat25 PSF option, while imexamine/psfmeasure fit beta (INDEF). Physically: T01 Sec. 2.4 attributes the broader wings of real PSFs to telescope optics as well as the atmosphere.

context_quotes.quote: the PSFs usually measured in real images have bigger "wings", or equivalently smaller values of β, than those expected from the turbulence theory (e.g. Saglia et al. 1993). This is because the real seeing not only depends on atmospheric conditions but is also caused by imperfections in telescope optics.

moffat_form.quote: with the full width at half maximum, FWHM=2α
moffat_form.note: The text layer drops the square-root sign and the superscript ("FWHM=2α 21/β - 1"); the formula is FWHM = 2 alpha sqrt(2^(1/beta) - 1). Unit total flux.
moffat_form.derived: DERIVED: alpha/FWHM = 1.2636 for beta = 4.765 and 0.8846 for beta = 2.5

fwhm_unobstructed.unit: lambda/D (radians on the sky; = 1.029 lambda f# in the focal plane)

fwhm_obstructed.status: NOT FOUND in a saved primary source as FWHM values; table is DERIVED
fwhm_obstructed.derived: DERIVED (computed here): annular pupil of outer diameter D and central obstruction eps (linear ratio), I(v) = I0 [2 J1(v)/v - eps^2 2 J1(eps v)/(eps v)]^2 / (1 - eps^2)^2 with v = pi D theta / lambda (standard annular-aperture Fraunhofer pattern; spiders ignored); FWHM from I = I(0)/2. Validation: the computed first-dark-ring radii reproduce Mahajan's tabulation (TOO, TABLE 10, row "Min.") to the 0.01 printed: 1.22, 1.21, 1.17, 1.11, 1.06, 1.00 lambda F for eps = 0-0.5.

validation_quote.loc: TABLE 10 (attributed to Mahajan, "Aberration Theory Made Simple"), first "Min." row; radius in units of lambda F
validation_quote.quote: TABLE 10 : EFFECT OF CENTRAL OBSTRUCTION ON NORMALIZED PSF INTENSITY DISTRIBUTION (Source: Aberration Theory Made Simple , Mahajan) ... Min. 1.22 1.21 1.17 1.11 1.06 1

context_quotes.quote: (3) reduction in the size of central maxima, by a ratio closely approximated with 1- o 2 + o 4
context_quotes.note: refers to the first-minimum size (eps = 0.5: 1 - eps^2 + eps^4 = 0.8125 vs DERIVED first-zero ratio 0.821); the FWHM shrinks less (ratio 0.886 at eps = 0.5)

context_quotes.quote: Pattern radius r is in units of λF

fwhm_obstructed.note: The core narrows with obstruction: about -2% at eps = 0.2, -5% at 0.3, -8% at 0.4, -11% at 0.5, while light moves into the rings (for the same source and outer diameter D the peak intensity falls by (1-eps^2)^2 relative to the clear aperture: (1-eps^2) from the lost collecting area times (1-eps^2) from the lower fraction of the light in the core). Searched ADS full text, arXiv and NASA NTRS: Mahajan (1986 JOSA A 3, 470) and Tschunko (1974 Appl. Opt. 13, 1820) treat this but are paywalled; no saved document quotes FWHM(eps). The explorer can compute the same numbers from the formula.
